title: Build a TCP echo server in Rust — 4 turns
description: Four-turn TCP server: turn 1 accept connections, turn 2 read/write echo protocol, turn 3 broadcast, turn 4 graceful shutdown and tests.

files.Cargo.toml:
[package]
name = "tcp-server"
version = "0.1.0"
edition = "2021"

[dependencies]
tokio = { version = "1", features = ["full"] }

task_spec.prompt: Implement `handle_echo(stream: TcpStream)` in `src/lib.rs`. Use `BufReader::new(stream)`, read lines with `read_line()`, and write each line back using `writer.write_all(line.as_bytes()).await`. Stop when the client disconnects (read_line returns 0 bytes). Run `cargo test --quiet test_echo`.
followup_prompts: Good progress. Run `cargo test --quiet` to see where we stand. Now implement `handle_broadcast(stream, tx)` — same as echo but instead of echoing back, broadcast each line with `tx.send(line)`. Also subscribe to `tx` and forward incoming broadcast messages to the client. Continue with the remaining steps.
Good. Now implement `Server::bind` properly — store the listener, and spawn an accept loop that calls `handle_broadcast` for each new connection. Run `cargo test --quiet` and fix any failures.
Final push: run `cargo test --quiet` and fix any remaining failures. Both tests must pass — echo and broadcast.
success_criteria: handle_echo reads lines and writes them back
handle_broadcast broadcasts each line to all subscribers
